explainBack.question: Why could NVIDIA owning Hugging Face affect which computing service your workplace's AI tool ends up using, even if alternatives stay listed?
explainBack.answer: Because finding a model and choosing who runs it are separate decisions, and the platform owner controls how easy each choice is. A model from the Hub still needs computing to do the work; the platform's defaults, documentation and pricing can quietly steer builders towards the owner's computing without removing rival services from the list. That is why the test is whether alternatives stay practical, not merely present.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: Reference to the catalogue/computing separation (P003, P006), the incentive tension of a computing supplier owning the catalogue (P007), and the practical-vs-listed distinction (P004, P012).
explainBack.assessment: The article's mechanism fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; no external knowledge was needed.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A browser maker announces it will acquire the most popular independent marketplace for browser extensions, promising that extensions will keep working on rival browsers and that developers can keep publishing for any browser.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, what should a workplace that relies on a marketplace extension check, beyond the promise itself?
unseenTransfer.answer: Separate the layers: the marketplace (catalogue), the browsers that actually run each extension (the computing analogue), and each extension's licence terms. Then test practicality over time: do install instructions, defaults and compatibility work start favouring the owner's browser; do rival-browser versions become harder to find or slower to update; do the terms for the workplace's intended use change? Ownership of the marketplace does not confer ownership of the extensions, but it can shape which choice is easy—so verify against published term changes and real switching effort, not the announcement.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Application of catalogue/runner/licence separation (P003, P006, P008), the distribution-influence mechanism (P005, P007), and the practical-choices test with dated follow-up (P004, P011).
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly to this novel situation absent from the piece, confirming it teaches a reusable model rather than a one-off story.
